evidence.detail: The exact-v308 class-file and recovered-source filename both preserve the unobfuscated public type name rs/secure/HardwareValidator / HardwareValidator.java.
Static initialization reads System.getProperty("os.name").toLowerCase(); the four predicates test Windows (win), macOS (mac), Unix/Linux (nix/nux/aix), and Solaris (sunos).
main(String[]) invokes the four predicates and prints exact surviving diagnostics 'This is Windows', 'This is Mac', 'This is Unix or Linux', 'This is Solaris', or 'Your OS is not support!!'.
The stable-ID sequence places this class immediately before R174's rs/secure/a,b,c providers at CLIENT_CLASS_000978..000980, fixing HardwareValidator as CLIENT_CLASS_000977.

candidates.note: Exact surviving source/class identity. The historical name is retained even though exact-v308 behavior is an OS/platform classifier rather than hardware validation in the ordinary sense.
